executive_assessment.text: NAP says drought can reduce water quantity and quality; many rural communities rely on a single river or stream, and resulting scarcity affects users across provinces.

Under the CCDR's BAU dry-hot scenario, drought risk rises fivefold by mid-century and climate change lowers annual GDP about 6 percent by 2050, affecting agriculture, hydropower and labor productivity.
CCDR says shock-responsive social protection backed by disaster risk financing has cushioned recent drought impacts; it recommends scaling early warning and adaptive social protection.

geographic_notes.text: Southern Province; Eastern Province; agro-ecological region I: NAP rates drought-related groundwater exposure high and says low-rainfall areas have lower adaptive capacity because droughts occur frequently, including Southern and Eastern provinces in agro-ecological region I.

Southern Province; Western Province; Eastern Province: NAP links drought yield losses to lower smallholder income from crop, livestock and fish sales, with little adaptation finance in Southern, Western and Eastern provinces.

Southern Province; Western Province; Eastern Province; Central Province: NAP states higher temperatures and drought contribute to more frequent forest-fire risk in Southern, Western, Eastern and Central provinces.
